children.text: Truck accidents are catastrophic and deadly. When an 80,000-pound big rig slams into a 3,000-pound passenger vehicle, the results are often tragic. Due to the sheer size and weight discrepancies between these two vehicles, occupants in passenger vehicles suffer the majority of the injuries. Even worse, their injuries are often life-threatening. After a truck accident, injured accident survivors may need to tend to their injuries and receive medical care. However, sometimes passengers are lucky enough to escape without serious and grave injuries. When this occurs, the steps they take after a serious truck accident can make a difference in their case. Even if you are unable to perform these steps, an
experienced Denver truck accident lawyer
can help you. Here are seven steps that our lawyers recommend you take after a truck accident.
Step One: Call 911

As mentioned above, truck accidents are serious and often result in fatal injuries. Therefore, anyone at the accident scene should immediately call 911 and report the crash. In the event of a serious crash, or a crash with a pedestrian or
bicycle

, calling emergency services immediately can be lifesaving. Reporting the accident alerts both the police and emergency medical teams. The faster injured passengers can receive medical help, the better. While injured accident victims receive life-saving medical help, the police will begin investigating and documenting the accident scene. This includes filling out a detailed police report with accurate information about all involved vehicles. The police report is an invaluable tool when seeking to file an accident claim.
Step Two: Gather Evidence

If the accident victim is seriously injured, then you can help by gathering evidence at the scene. This means snapping pictures of the crash damage, the road debris, and any other important factors. Be sure to take pictures of the scene from multiple angles. (Only do this if it is safe to walk around the scene.) If you are able, then collect contact information for anyone who may have witnessed the accident.
Step Three: Collect Contact Information
It is important to exchange contact information with other drivers involved in the crash. Some of this information includes:
Insurance cards, including policy numbers
Driver’s license numbers
Driver’s home address, phone number, and email address
License plate numbers
Contact information for the truck driver’s employer and trucking company
Identifying information about the truck and other vehicles involved
Step Four: Vehicle Appraisal

Any settlement you accept must include sufficient money to repair your vehicle accurately. As such, a repair estimate is an important part of the insurance claim process. Every insurance company has their own requirements for getting vehicle damage appraised. Even still, you have the right to have your vehicle appraised by your own company, as well as the body shop your insurance company requests. Yet, be careful not to let your body shop perform work on your car until after you speak to your attorney and the insurance company.
Step Five: Speak to Insurance Agents

Most insurance policies require policyholders to let them know when an accident occurs. While you may need to call your insurance company to report the accident, be careful about what you say. Also, if the trucking company’s insurance company calls, then be polite. However, do not talk about the details of the accident or your case. It is important to speak to a truck accident lawyer before speaking to the insurance company and giving them a statement. Insurance adjusters will look for any reason to reduce or deny your claim. As such, call an attorney before speaking to the insurance company.
Step Six: Avoid Social Media

It is tempting to post about your accident on social media. However, it is best to avoid social media altogether after a truck accident. Even simple pictures and phrases are often used against accident survivors in court. Insurance companies may claim that these pictures show that the survivors are not as injured as they claim. For example, consider the phrase, “I was in a truck accident today. Luckily I am not too injured.” Insurance companies could claim that you admitted to not suffering an injury after the accident, which could hurt your case in court. As such, avoid posting on social media until after you accept a settlement.
